utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you, General, the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jovanovski. Do you remember, General, that we ended yesterday's evidence by you clarifying to me the position of posebna and the fact that you, too, as the superior of posebna were subordinated to the army of the Republic of Macedonia in the fights in May 2001. Do you recall having said that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, battles, instead of fights.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at the court file in -- Roman IV, tab 16, Exhibit P75, R 002 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] R0424692, and the same number E appended in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, this is the decision to establish the posebna unit of the police of the Ministry of the Interior of the 26th of June, 2001. And now I would like to ask you to turn at R0424695, and the English page is the last page, R042-4694-ET. And I kindly ask you to look at paragraph 15 where you can see that when this decision enters into force the validity of the decision passed on the 2nd of June, 2003 is terminated; so do you agree with me that this decision shows and confirms what you testified about that posebna existed for a number of years before the -- this decision was passed? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the second page of this decision, that is, R042-4693, Macedonian page, and the English page R042-4693-ET. Actually, I apologise, it will be 4692-ET. It is the paragraph 6 here that I wish to show to you, and ask you about it. The Article 6 specifies the command and -- the commanding and the basic composition of the posebna unit and it states that the -- what is posebna unit made of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The paragraph 2 of this item 6 speaks about the composition of the Battalion Skopje. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the office you held in 2001, first in the posebna and then in the police department, during the brief meeting with you I showed you the structure of the posebna Battalion Skopje and you stated that you knew, in general, what this battalion was and what was its composition.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look in this binder at the tab 19, which is 65 ter 1D551.2, page 1D5065, while the English is 1D5066. You see here correspondence from the Central Police Services, which they submit upon the request of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski under the item 3, formation inventory of the battalion of posebna, Skopje for the period of July/August 2001. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 20, that is 65 ter 1D552 and that is the page 1D5067, and the English is 1D5080. This is, General, the list of all members of the posebna battalion for Skopje as of July and August 2001. Are you familiar with the composition of this battalion, also in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that the composition of this battalion established in June 2001 was not changed at least until the autumn of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some five per cent of the members might have been replaced, due to justified reasons such as sickness or if they left abroad or something, but the commanding structure of this unit was unchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you could accept that the information that the Ministry of the Interior provided that this composition was unchanged in July and August is correct. You could accept that information as correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering these facts, the Defence moves to have these two documents received as Defence exhibits, 65 ter 1D551.2, and 65 ter 1D552.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be exhibit number 1D151 for 65 ter 1D00551.2, and exhibit number 1D152, marked for identification for 65 ter 1D00552.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understood that you stated that the exhibits are received, while I think that the transcript reads that they are marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, are you familiar with the name of Goran Gjorgievski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was the head of the department for posebna units in the police department of the Ministry of the Interior in July and August 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, General, that on the 12th of August, late in the afternoon, there was a risk of a huge clash and high casualties at Radisanski road between the villagers of Ljuboten who were moving towards Skopje and the villagers from the neighbouring villages in the Skopje vicinity who were armed with various instruments and who arrived there in that area. Did you have that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know, General, that in the afternoon, late in the afternoon of that day, General Risto Galevski issued an order to send part of posebna to that region to protect the people, to separate them, and to enable peaceful return of the Ljuboten villagers to their village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the police jargon, it is called a tampon zone, between two crowds of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that order was communicated to Goran Gjorgievski, the leader of posebna, the superior of posebna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, if someone, if some document would state that on the 12th of August the Lions were sent to Ljuboten to separate the crowds, what would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand. Could you repeat it? I had problems with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, my question is, first, let's go step by step. Are you sure that on that day, upon the order of General Galevski the posebna unit was sent to the area near Radisani?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if someone would state or if some document would state that it was not posebna, the unit which was sent but the Lions instead, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't any such document and the Lions were not established at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this would be absolutely impossible because you have just stated that the Lions had not existed still then. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I would like to ask you now to talk about the Lions for a while and there were several witnesses who have testified about this issue before this Court, and numerous documents were received in evidence. Therefore, I will ask you only some specific questions to clarify several issues related to the Lions. I would like to ask to you look now at the table that is in tab Roman numeral V, number 22. This is Exhibit P74, the page is R042-4682, and the English version is 042-4682-ET-01. General, this is a decision of the Ministry of Interior dated 6th of August, 2001, and that is a decision to establish a rapid intervention police battalion of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the page 2 of this document, that is R042-4683, and the English page is - let me just look at the number - 042-4682-ET-02. And I would ask you to look together at the item 4 of this decision. First I would like to ask you whether you know that the Minister Boskoski, on the basis of the decision of the president of the republic and the decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia issued a decision to establish a rapid interventions battalion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is this the decision that we have in front of us now?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this decision establishes the tasks, the procedure of establishment, the composition. Is this what we can see from this decision, if you look at it closely?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the item 4 that I wish to draw your attention. The first paragraph says that the police battalion will be -- rapid intervention police battalion will be populated on a voluntary basis and by secondment from the posebna unit of the Ministry of Interior. Is this the first basis or the first source from which the rapid interventions battalion was established?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree, since we spoke about it before, that these members of posebna were actually regular employees with full employment status in the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph reads: "Members of the rapid intervention police battalion from the reserve forces of the Ministry of the Interior will enter into employment contract with the Ministry of the Interior." Does this mean, am I able to understand it well, that the second source from which the rapid interventions battalion will be populated are the reserve forces of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I wish to ask you to confirm if it is correct that, actually, the reserve forces of the police did not have a full employment status with the Ministry of the Interior when they were only reservists. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reserve forces are called up only in a complex situation or when they need to have a drill and they do not have a full employment status with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, the rapid interventions battalion comprised two parts or was composed out of two parts from the Ministry of Interior: The first one were the members who already had employment status, and who belonged to the posebna unit; and the second part came from the members of the Ministry of Interior and they were the activated reserve forces who, until, their enrolment in the rapid interventions battalion, did not have full employment status with the ministry. Is this understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these police officers from the posebna and who had employment status and also the reserve forces, so the persons who became members of the reserve forces, they were deployed to various crisis regions as early as the beginning of the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look -- to show a video. That is Exhibit P227.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would mention for the transcript, Ms. Residovic that apparently that was Exhibit P277, not Exhibit P227.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. So this is Exhibit P277; I apologise. And the transcript of this video recording is in the binder in tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you can see from this video that this was a parade of the police units. Were you present there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was in November 2001. Is that correct? At Penus?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what the Minister Boskoski stated, the Tigers and -- and the posebna unit and the Lions stood at attention there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister mentioned that they were fighting for nine months. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is now, General: Considering that we stated that the Lions were created from the existing police, posebna, and the regular forces, that since the beginning of the crisis, participated in the fights in the crisis regions. If I were to say that when the minister stated that those who fought for nine months, would that quote mean that they fought in the composition of the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's unclear in this question to which police force Ms. Residovic is referring to. Posebna, Tigers, or Lions, because I believe they were all mentioned or shown in that -- in that video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters wish to note that there is interference in our headsets which is growing louder, so if something could be done about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister says that they were fighting for nine months and the journalists were saying - and I wish to thank my learned friend for correcting me - that here were the members of the Tigers as well. I apologise, by the minister said only nine months. However, in the further text from the text that follows, that is in front of the witness and mentioned the Tigers and other defenders. I really apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to reformulate the question that I would like to put forward to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, General, when the minister mentioned that they were fighting for nine months whether, regardless of who is -- who is present here, whether the members of the Lions who had been members of the posebna and their reserve forces, were they also participating for nine month in the battles within the composition of the posebna or within the composition of the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Rapid Intervention Unit was established, as you mentioned, it was consisted of police officers, reserve force members and other members of the posebna unit. We did not receive many more from the posebna nor from the reserve forces who in the nine month preceding were distinguished or exemplified themselves and proved to be very good in dealing with certain weapons or vehicles and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, we received the major number of people from the posebna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I were to say that among the Lions, when they were established, there was nobody else in it other than the already existing members of the police whether from the posebna or whether from the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No paramilitary groups became part of the Lions, regardless of the fact whether they existed anywhere in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before entering in the Ministry of Interior, before somebody is hired by the Ministry of Interior, we run background checks. These background checks had to be passed by anybody. There was not a single person who had been a member of any kind of organisation that was hired.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday my learned friend the Prosecutor showed you a video that showed the signing of the contract, the hiring contract, of the members of the Rapid Intervention Battalion. Do you remember seeing this movie yesterday when the Prosecutor showed you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember watching the video but do not recall exactly whether that was the signing of the employment contracts because it was interrupted. We didn't see it fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very correct. However, bearing in mind the position that you held, you know that before this event and according -- pursuant to the decision for the establishment of the Rapid Intervention Battalion with the reserve forces, that had already undergone the procedure that was prescribed by the rule book, that with these individuals, that these individuals entered into an employment contract with the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask to you look at this document, which is right after tab 30. This is 65 ter 222, the page is N000-5388, and the English one, the English page is N000-5388-ET. And here you can see the list of individuals between 1 and 182, and the title says: Review of 182 persons that were employed in the Rapid Intervention Battalion, Lavovi, Lions, based on received concurrence by the ministry of finance, number 19-6201/4, dated the 12th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since this unit was within the police organisational structure please tell me whether are these individuals and the time at which these members of the reserve forces, after the procedure was implemented were hired and thus became members of the Lions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I propose that this -- I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be exhibit number 1D153.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering this document relating to which I asked you several questions, would it be correct to say, General, that the procedure of establishing the Lions started with the decision of the minister from August 6, 2001 and continued -- ended at the -- at the middle of November 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If there had been a document that said something to the effect that there were groups known as Lions who had been participating in the battles in Tetovo on June 2, 2001, then those groups had -- in case they had existed, had nothing to do with the police units, with the Ministry of Interior, nor with the Minister Boskoski. Would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to show the witness part of the testimonies of the protected witness who had already testified in front of this Court. So maybe we should move on to a semi-closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, we spoke about the units of the police who were within your department. On several occasions, you mentioned the reserve police forces. And if I were to tell you that in some certain situations, in the cases where the security situation is worsened and there is an immediate security problems or war, the reserve force of the police are activated. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During peacetime, part of the military conscripts is determined to be part of those within -- to be within the reserve police forces.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are lists which, in peacetime, are kept in a safe and from time to time these members are invited for some activities and as you have mentioned yourself when the situation gets complicated they are called upon to be reservists in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, the situation was such that required activation of the reserve police forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the army called upon those individuals who were designated to come from the reserve army forces.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The army also has reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the police did not have enough number of individuals within its own reserve forces, then the secretariat of Defence or the secretariat of Defence would need to second the reserve forces from the military or the civilian protection into the police reserve forces. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not have civil defence anymore. But, yes, from the army, from the military, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, the crisis were of such dimensions that a number of the reserve forces who had been previously designated for the police it was not enough. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because of this, there was a public announcement for people to volunteer in the police reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, as an answer to one of the questions, you said that the rule book regulates the manner through which invitations are extended and that this procedure is realised by individuals who in the Ministry of Interior work in the area of defence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the ministry there is a department for defence preparations and each inspector has his or her area of work and they have to call upon a certain number of people and there is a rule book according to which they invite those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after the general decision for activating the reserve forces those individuals who work in the area of defence preparations have the responsibility to invite the reserve police forces or to second it, according to the law and the rule book they do not need any additional orders. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They have their orders sealed in envelopes and when the reserve police force is activated those envelopes are opened and they can see inside what they need to do and how they to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to look at what's behind tab 34. It is 65 ter 1D209, the page is R042-4704, and the English one is R042-4704 also. This is the draft of the -- of the -- it's a draft English translation. General, this is from the official gazette of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this the Book of Rules that regulates the manner through which the reserve forces are summoned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D154.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you started saying that it is not enough that somebody has weapons to become a member of the reserve forces, if I understood well. However, regardless of what you tried to say something about yesterday, I would now like to ask you: In order to become a member of the reserve forces of the Republic of Macedonia, is it true that it is necessary, first, for a person to respond to a summons or to volunteer in case the summons were public?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then, to -- for weapons and uniform to be issued?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then, to go through a brief training which, in 2001, took place in Idrizovo, to receive the ID from the reserve forces, and to be put on the payroll in order to receive the remuneration for the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the members of the reserve forces are involved for more than one month, and that person -- that person's regular job is put on hold and he receives his salary from the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody received a uniform or weapons in any part of the Ministry of the Interior, whether by virtue of only this, would this person become a member of the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the work of the committee that you chaired, you obtained the list from the police station for the security of facilities and persons that had a number of -- the number of 84 persons who received weapons and uniform at this police station. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If these individuals had never been entered into the list of the reserve forces, if they had not been remunerated, and if they had not been in the list of those individuals that received training in Idrizovo, would it be correct for me to say that they were not in the reserve police forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now like to -- you to look at the document past tab 39. That is Exhibit 1D118, page is 1D4454, and the English one is 1D4456. In this information, the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia submits to the Defence of Mr. Boskoski the ministry confirms that those -- those individuals from the PSOLO list from the 25th and the 26th of July were not members of the police reserve forces. They had not been remunerated, that the ministry does not have any documents that they participated in the Idrizovo training, and they had not been issued with any police ID?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document confirm with what you just told me that they were not members of the police forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When working in the second committee, you also received a list of persons who were allegedly issued weapons at the Cair police station. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 41. That is 65 ter 1D00554.1, the page is 1D00-5101. It enumerates eight individuals regarding which the Defence of Mr. Boskoski requests the ministry to answer whether these persons have been remunerated, whether they have received remuneration from the Ministry of the Interior in 2001. I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 42. That is 65 ter 1D554.2, 1D5103, and the English version is 5104. And this is a response that the cabinet of the state secretary in the Ministry of the Interior in Skopje sends to the Defence of Mr. Boskoski and which indicates that the persons enumerated in the correspondence from us were not registered in the payroll of the ministry, and thus far they were never remunerated from the Ministry of the Interior. Considering this fact, General, sir, could you say that these persons haven't been members of the reserve forces of the police either?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender these two documents 1D554.2 and 1D554.1 as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my concern, and it's a concern that I've raised previously, is whether such a letter from the Ministry of the Interior is really the equivalent of a witness statement and whether this should become -- and should be exhibited in this case. The questions and answers have been read into the record, so the Prosecution is simply wondering whether, based on the normal practice of this trial, these documents should be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The letters will not be received as exhibits, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague yesterday, you stated that you knew about the protests of citizens of the reserve forces and the army on the 25th of June, 2001 in Skopje. Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the minister, after the events and wishing to support the programme of peaceful resolution of the crisis, had adopted a decision to perform the deactivation, demobilisation of the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that the president of the Republic reacted to such decision of the minister and requested that this decision is annulled?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on these facts, General, sir, could you agree with me if I say that the president of the Republic of Macedonia performing the competences vested to him by the constitution and the law, issued decision about the use of police forces for combat purposes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, about what really happened in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001, and briefly only, since there were other witnesses who had already testified about this. Is it correct that the crisis in Macedonia started with the attacks of some sabotage terrorist groups in January 2001 in the area of Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three members of our forces were killed then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after that, the attacks continued, the attacks of these sabotage terrorist groups, and also in some areas of Tetovo, Kumanovo and later in Skopje they gained in intensity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These sabotage terrorist groups attacked the police stations and police patrols, military facilities but also civilian facilities, workers going to work, as well as the general population.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And during that time, pressurised by these terrorist attacks, huge number or proportion of Macedonian population needed to leave their homes in the areas of Tetovo and Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Skopje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the ways, with the terrorist methods that the NLA used most frequently during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I attempt to summarize them, would those be kidnapping and holding civilians as hostages, both Macedonians and Albanians; kidnapping and holding hostage members of the Macedonian security forces; ill-treatment -- physical ill-treatment and intimidation; killing; destruction of private and religious facilities; and similar activities. Would those be some of the methods that were used by the NLA in the activities against security forces and the people in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: One of the frequent methods that the NLA used during that time was to place or to lay minefields against the Macedonian forces and to mine roads, in order to cause casualties in both the civilians and the security forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would mine roads. They did not make a distinction whether it would be civilians or security forces who would use those roads.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone would claim that the NLA did not use minefields, would such assertion be accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that these sabotage terrorist groups built their power mainly on the intimidation of the population and controlling part of that region physically, armed by weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that frequently the police, in consultations with representatives of the international community withdrew from the police stations in order to avoid casualties in the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the security forces of Macedonia, both the police and the army, a special problem was that the NLA members, mingled, mixed with the civilian population, which prevented the security forces from having a more energetic reaction because they wanted to avoid civilian casualties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Macedonian authorities tried to evacuate the civilian population before the start of the military operations in order to avoid human casualties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document which is found in tab 8, number 61. That is 65 ter 1D559, 1D5124, and we have this document in the English language only, and I -- first let me say that this is Associated Press and Reuters news services, dated 8th of May, 2001. And let us look at the page 1D2128.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: 5128. If you look towards the middle, yes, towards the middle of this page, it reads 05-07845, and the title is Bush administration expresses support for Macedonia. The paragraph 2 reads: "[In English] Bush supports the efforts of the government of Macedonia to fight the extremists who have brought the violence to the region. White House press secretary Ari Fleischer said. Bush met last week with Macedonian president Boris Trajkovski in Washington and told him, Fleischer said, that the ultimate answer to Macedonia's ethnic strife must be a political solution. But, added Fleischer, the president wants to make certain that Macedonia is able to take the action they need to combat a problem that has been created by the extremists." [Interpretation] So given this support that the President Bush extends to the Macedonian president, it can be clearly seen that the Macedonian authorities were supported in resolving the crisis situation and that they are also advised to look for a political solution for the problem. Does this -- can this be inferred from this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further in the text it is stated: "[In English] Macedonian troops launched a weekend offensive, forcing ethnic Albanian rebels to flee across a nearby border into Kosovo while the government ordered residents of several villages to evacuate and claimed the rebels were holding hundreds of civilians as human shields." [Interpretation] Does this information corroborate what you stated before, that the Macedonian authorities tried to safeguard and protect the civilian population but the NLA frequently used the civilian population as human shield?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was most strikingly visible in the Kumanovo region and in the Skopje region, one may say, where the Albanian population was held hostage in the basement. They were not allowed to leave the village or go out of the houses. They were used as human shield.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document in evidence as Defence exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number 1D155.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now, General, to look at the next document in tab 62. That is, again, a Associated Press and Reuters news services. This time dated May 17th, 2001 and that is 65 ter 1D560, page 1D5136. In the penultimate paragraph, this first page, it reads: "[In English] Reuters, Macedonian president Boris Trajkovski urged civilians on Wednesday to leave rebel-held villages, warning that the army was about to use decisive force to drive out ethnic Albanian guerillas." [Interpretation] General, was this the constant, the permanent way in which the authorities of the Republic of Macedonia, before they start a military action, attempted to remove and to protect the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this document in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit 1D156.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you've just mentioned that this -- that the civilians, especially in the Kumanovo region, were used as human shield. Yesterday, when asked or -- alongside a conclusion of my learned friend the Prosecutor, we learned that you were injured severely?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That happened in Vaksince, in the Kumanovo region. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the methods of minefields, minefields that would kill or wound the Macedonian security forces, were the way where the NLA was active in that region as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there also, the Albanians who cooperated with the Macedonian authorities were intimidated and particularly the police officers who worked at the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We even had information that in the Tetovo village of Poroj [phoen] there was a public execution of an Albanian who had cooperated with the police bodies, and it was never reported anywhere and it was not stated publicly that it was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And NLA used these methods throughout the crisis, and it did not refrain from using them, even after the signing of the Ohrid framework agreement when some of the NLA groups ONA, Macedonian abbreviation, were renamed ANA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I don't know whether you have the information that few days ago, when Albanian commander of a police station was again killed at Vaksince performing his duties as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour. Objection, Your Honour. I don't see the relevance of that question or the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, what is the relevance? We are dealing with events in 2001. We're certainly not going to try the political situation in Macedonia in 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I'm now speaking about methods of the NLA and the security situation and the possibilities for the Minister Boskoski to have entered the village of Ljuboten until May 2001, that was my intention in mentioning this. The events before and the developments after the signing of the agreement, if it was understood differently, I then apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question appears to be speaking about recent events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will not be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will now adjourn for the first break, to resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We understand there is some issues counsel which to raise. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon. There are indeed two very short matters. The first one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'll record the time when you said it will be very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will apply my own definition of very short, Your Honour. The first has to do with the repeat ruling prior to the break by the Trial Chamber concerning the non-admission of two documents which were numbered as Rule 65 ter 1D554.1 and.2 respectively. Your Honour, those documents are indeed important, we submit and the Defence will seek to tender the information contained in those documents; however, in view of the Trial Chamber's ruling of a moment ago, the Defence would like to seek brief clarification from the Trial Chamber with a view to ensure that when the information contained in those document is sought to be tendered in a different form, they could indeed be tendered. What the Defence has in mind, perhaps, and if it is agreeable to the Trial Chamber, would be to submit those in the form of a Rule 92 bis statement taken from the person in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I answer you quite quickly and simply without having to turn to Mr. Saxon, if he does not mind. If you want to prove a fact, you lead evidence to prove it. If you want to prove that certain people were employed or were not employed in a ministry of the government, you lead evidence to prove it. A letter from the ministry to counsel could suggest that was the case, but does not go far enough to prove it. To prove it, either a witness who was here for some other reason may have sufficient personal knowledge to be able to say what it is that you want proved. Alternatively, you call a witness, who does know from the ministry who can say that. As an alternative to calling the witness, you may seek to use the Rule 92 bis procedure, that is getting a proper form statement from a witness who knows, and see whether then there is on a motion to have it received as a statement, see whether or not there is any difficulty to be found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely. And that clarifies the matter. Your Honour, the second issue which we would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber concerns a number of documents, or rather, records of minutes of meetings between the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on the one hand and representative of the Macedonian authorities. We understand from our investigation and from the disclosure which we have received from the Prosecution that there were a number of such meetings in the years 2001 and 2002. As part of the disclosure material, we have received several records in various forms of those meetings, several of which were in the forms of so-called investigator's notes. We have already used, actually, two of those documents, Your Honour, with the witness Dr. Jakovski. The Defence has become aware, however, that the records of a number of other meetings between the OTP and representatives of the Macedonian authorities in relation to the investigation of the Ljuboten matter in 2001 and 2002, had not been disclosed to the Defence. On 19 August of this year, we have, therefore, written a letter to senior trial attorney Mr. Saxon with a view to obtain the records of those meetings, in particular, we had identified three such meetings: On the 20th and 21st of November of 2001; a second meeting on the 22nd of March of 2002; and a third meeting on the 8th of May of 2002. On the 21st of August, Mr. Saxon indicated to the Defence that this material would not be disclosed to the Defence on the basis that this material, the Prosecution suggested, fell under Rule 70 A. The Prosecution did not indicate that the material did not exist or that it was otherwise not relevant to the proceedings. On the 22nd of August, the Defence wrote, once again, to the Prosecutor asking the OTP, essentially, to reconsider its position. On the 7th of September, Mr. Saxon again responded to the Defence reiterating the position of the office that the documents in question fell under Rule 70 A. According to the Defence, this position is without merit. The suggestion by the Prosecution may that such material and information could fall or would fall within this Rule 70 A can easily be set aside. I have already indicated that approximately two dozen similar documents were already provided to the Defence pursuant to Rule 66 and/or Rule 68 by the Prosecution in various forms, mainly in the forms of investigator' notes. The only difference which seemed to appear between those documents which have been disclosed to the Defence and those which the Prosecution declines to be disclosed to the Defence is the presence of the chief Prosecutor Madam Del Ponte at the three meetings in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What about their content?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well their content, Your Honour, is made evident, if I may use that term, from other documents which we have received from the Prosecution or from material which is publicly available. I will give you an example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point I'm making is, there are meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The rule says what isn't discoverable are matters in connection with the investigation or preparation of the case. Now a great variety of things can be dealt with at meetings. If the Prosecution is made a lot available to you that says of others, These come within Rule 70 A, the content of the meeting or the document may be the big point of differentiation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we have reason, if I understand your question properly, we understand that those meetings indeed related to the Ljuboten investigation. For instance, the meeting of the 20th and 21st of November was a meeting organised specifically for the visit of Madam Del Ponte in Macedonia. A video was made of some parts of that meeting, Madam Del Ponte was seen, among other things shaking the hands of Mr. Boskoski during that meeting and it is indicated from other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What has that got to do with anything, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There have been at times during this trial by all sides things thrown in like this, which really are not going to help anybody, are they.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What we believe the relevance of that, Your Honour, is that it is the Prosecution case that during the period from the 12th of August onwards until sometime in May of 2002, Mr. Boskoski failed in his duties which the Prosecution claims he had to do particular things, what the Defence believe is that these records and these documents may reveal material which is relevant to this question, in particular, whether any assistance was sought or given by Mr. Boskoski. Thus, my reference to the presence of Mr. Boskoski during the meeting with Madam Del Ponte and other meetings of that sort where, for instance, the question of exhumation or autopsies were being discussed which, again, is an issue relevant to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If your client was present, he knows what transpired at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we have sought to obtain the records from the other side, so to say, from the Macedonian authorities and unfortunately haven't been able to do so. At this stage short of calling Mr. Boskoski to give evidence about this matter, we would have no alternative but to seek either the documents in question from the Prosecution or to seek to interview some of the participants in those meetings. We believe that the easiest way in this and the quickest course in this matter is to have the record themselves provided to the Defence to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the other indication, Your Honour, which we would like to make at this stage in relation to the suggestion by the Prosecution that this is -- that the records of meetings or the notes taken by the Prosecutor of meetings with individuals related to the case would fall under Rule 70 A goes not only to contrary to the material which has been already disclosed closed to the Defence as I indicated, but also contrary to some of the material which the Prosecution itself is seeking to use. And I will simply refer here to Rule 65 ter 783, 784 and 785, which likewise are so-called investigator notes which, in essence, are notes taken by the Prosecution of particular meeting between a representative of the Prosecution and third parties. As for the relevance, Your Honour, I think I have indicated essentially what we believed could be relevant to this matter. In particular, the circumstances under which the investigation was carried out at the time, what was being done at the time, what couldn't be done at the time, what the position of the Macedonian authorities were at the time, and if any request was made to Mr. Boskoski for assistance in relation to this matter. I will give the floor to Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a moment, please, Mr. Saxon. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honours, I should say, the -- Mr. Mettraux is quite correct when he explains to the Chamber that the Prosecution has told Defence counsel that it will not disclose these notes of meetings that were held with Madam Del Ponte, the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, and leaders of the Macedonian government because, in the Prosecution's submission, such notes are protected by Rule 70 A. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that has got to depend upon their content.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'm sorry. What is correct is that was the communication made by the Prosecution to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where the Prosecution parts company with the Defence on this matter is with Mr. Mettraux's submission that the Prosecution's argument that Rule 70 A applies is somehow contrary or inconsistent with other disclosures made by the Prosecution to the Defence, pursuant to either Rule 66 B or Rule 68. It is true, Your Honours, that the Prosecution has disclosed other materials that describe meetings between members of the Office of the Prosecutor and persons working in Macedonia, such as the members of the forensic institute, and the OSCE who, during late 2001 and early 2002 were planning the exhumations in the Ljuboten cemetery that eventually took place in May 2002. And specifically and primarily I'm referring to notes of meetings in which future Prosecution witness, Mr. Howard Tucker participated and made some notes. However, Your Honour, in the Prosecution's submission, there is a large qualitative difference between notes made by a Prosecution investigator related to ongoing investigations in this case and notes made of high-level, often sensitive meetings undertaken by the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, Ms. Del Ponte involving discussions with government leaders including leaders of the state of Macedonia. Secondly, Your Honour, I have reviewed the notes of such meetings and in the Prosecution's opinion, there is nothing in those notes that falls within the Prosecution's disclosure obligations underneath the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you please elaborate what you're saying about notes of meetings between, as we understand it, the Prosecutor, and members of the Macedonian government or very senior officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the content of those is not discoverable because the content is not within the scope of Rule 66 or Rule 68, or are you saying it's not discoverable because it is protected by Rule 70 A?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm saying both, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And in either case, then, what is the point of the distinction you're making between investigators's notes of meetings and notes of high-level meetings involving the Prosecutor? I couldn't grasp what that had to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the Prosecution's submission, Your Honour, and if I can say in the OTP's submission, the particular meetings, discussions that are undertaken by the Prosecutor herself, she often meets with heads of states, she has often meetings on extremely delicate matters and in the Prosecution's submission, such notes normally should fall within the protection of Rule 70 A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If those -- the discussions at those meetings contain discoverable material or disclosable material under Rule 68 or 66, they should be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Point taken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's why I was confused by you introducing that factor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If they are discussions at a high level about generalities and are not discussions that deal with any matter that comes within the terms of Rule 66 or 68, there is no issue. There's then the question of Rule 70 A about which it is still not clear to me what it is you're saying. Are you saying here that there is material here that was to do with the investigation and preparation of the Prosecution's case for this trial, or is that not the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The position seems to have been a little confused by some responses given by the Prosecutor in this case, but the position, as clarified, in response to Mr. Mettraux's application, is that no -- the prosecuting counsel leading in this case has examined the documents in question, and none of them are subject to disclosure in his assessment under Rule 66 or Rule 68. The Defence are not able to identify or specify in what respect there's material in these documents which is either wrongly appreciated by the Prosecutor or which is, in some way, relevant to their case and which they ought to have to enable them to properly prepare their case for trial. The assurance of counsel that we have is the normal basis upon which matters of this nature are finally assessed. Unless there is something about the nature of the document that is known or the circumstances which indicate that there is reason to think that the document really ought to be disclosed, because it's material to the preparation of the Defence. In this case, the Chamber is unable to see that there is any such indication in anything that is before us. We would further observe that insofar as they were present at these meetings, both the Prosecutor of this Chamber and the accused Mr. Boskoski, what transpired at the meetings is therefore within the knowledge of Mr. Boskoski. Despite that, it is still not able to be advanced how or in what particular the content of these documents ought to be disclosed. In those circumstances, the oral motion is refused. Is there any other matter? We'd better have the witness back. Just short of 30 minutes is the answer to the question of what is a short time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, is it correct that through those information that came from the public security of the municipality of Cair and especially from the continuous information from the administration for counter-intelligence and security, could you have found out that Ljuboten, from the very beginning of the crisis, was used as a logistics base from the NLA forces in Skopska Crna Gora?

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Although this was mentioned several times in front of this Court, can you confirm that Skopska Crna Gora and the position of Ljuboten of an exceptional strategic importance for the city Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask to you look at a document right after the tab 843. That is exhibit 1D142. The Macedonian page is N006-3880 and the English one is -- I apologise, the other page is 1D43709. And the English one is 1D4711. This is tab 43 in your binder.

utterances.text: General, as you can see, this is a document from the administration of public security Skopje and it represents -- it has a very interesting understanding. The Defence received this from the Prosecutor. Is this one type of a document that the administration for public security -- from the state security sent besides the designated individuals in the document also to the headquarters Ramno to inform them of their intelligence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will ask to you look at page 2 of this document. And as I said, this is a document from 28 February 2001. Page 2 of the document both in the English it's the -- it is still on the first page. The last paragraph of the first page. And the second paragraph of the second page in the Macedonian version. It says the following: "We received the operational information that in the area of Basinec above Ljuboten village, a large-scale movement of the population was observed during the day and throughout the night there were guards were organised around the installation in the area." utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to you look at the information past the tab 44. This is it document 65 ter 1D555, page 1D5105; the English 1D5107. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender these documents in evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Now I would like to ask to you look at the document after the tab 45, Exhibit 1D143, and the page is N005-7390. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you can see in the middle of the second paragraph it says: "At the same time, the source stated that some of these individuals regularly go down to the village of Ljuboten using motor vehicles, as well as to Skopje. utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at the document past tab 46. That is a document 65 ter 1016, number N005-7408, and the English one is N005-7408-ET, page 1. In the second paragraph of the both Macedonian and the English version: "The 16th, the 17th and the 18th of March in 2001, in the village of Ljuboten, people in civilian clothes came to urge the local population to join the terrorists. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D158.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now again to look beside -- after the tab 48. It is document 65 ter 1D596, page 1, N005-7438. General, this time in front of you, you can see -- you can see the operational intelligence from the operational worker collected by the department -- the administration for security from the municipality of Cair. And it represents the content of the conversation that the authorised inspector undertake -- undertook on the 28th of June, 2001. In Article 1, in the middle of it which says: "Namely --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it begins with the words: "It was also noticed."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says: "It was also noticed that a bigger quantity of sand was brought in several turns to the courtyards of two houses in Ljuboten village. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document in evidence as well.

utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D159.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at document at tab 50. This is a document, 65 ter 1D597, page 1 on the Macedonian version, and 65 ter 1019, page 1. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]

utterances.text: General, can you confirm that within the administration for security and counter-intelligence there was also a sector for analytics that was undertaking analysis information and assessments of the security situation?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to look at the document at tab 61. This is document 65 ter 1D598, page 1. It is the same page in English. The number is N005-7467. utterances.text: This is -- this was in August 2001.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering that in the document on page N005-7451, the situation in Ljuboten is analysed and the General is in a position to be able to recognise the documents as documents from the administration for security and counter-intelligence, I seek to tender this document in evidence of the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D162.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC

Presevo valley is at the south of Serbia. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the three-partied border between Kosovo, Serbia and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document confirms that the illegal transfer of weapons also went both through the village and by the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 55. That is 65 ter document 1D520, page 1D4748, Macedonian, while 1D4749, the English. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]

Does this corroborate what you had, the information that you had, in terms of certain number of people from Ljuboten having participated in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D164.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 56, General. utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 1D165.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now look at the document in tab 57, General. That is 65 ter 1D557, page number 1D5114, and the English version is 1D5116. Do you agree that this document also corroborates the presence of the NLA members in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document in evidence as a Defence exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: The last paragraph of this document, last paragraph at this page in the Macedonian language, and it is also the last paragraph in the English version page, is the complete organisation of taking over and storing of the mentioned weapons was carried out by the person Alimi Baki, known under the nickname Commander Lisi.
